lines.text: Almost 20% of the Netherlands is water.
There are many rivers.
The Rhine [Rijn] comes from Germany, the Meuse [Maas] comes from Belgium.
The largest lake is the IJsselmeer.
It used to be a sea.
That sea was closed off with the closure dike [Afsluitdijk], which is thirty kilometers long.
The Netherlands lies on the North Sea [Noordzee].
North of the Afsluitdijk lies the Waddenzee with the Wadden Islands [Waddeneilanden].
The largest Wadden Island is called Texel.
In old cities, such as Amsterdam and Utrecht, there are canals [grachten] with old houses.
"Nederland" means "low land." A large part of the west lies below sea level [zeespiegel]: the land is lower than the sea.
The lowest point is close to Rotterdam, as much as seven meters below sea level.
The water has advantages [voordelen]: Rotterdam has the largest port in Europe, there is a lot of transport on the rivers, and there are many experts in building bridges, dikes and ships.
There are also disadvantages [nadelen]: throughout history there have been many floods [overstromingen].
This is how the Netherlands protects itself against the water:
Along the North Sea there are dunes [duinen], made by nature.
Where there are no dunes, the Dutch have built dikes [dijken], for example along the rivers and in Zeeland.
A dike lies between land and water.
There are also dams [dammen], for example in Zeeland.
A dam lies between water and water.
There are many polders: land that used to be water, usually below sea level, with dikes around it.
The province of Flevoland is almost entirely polder.
Many windmills are polder mills [poldermolens].
In the past they were important for pumping [pompen] water away from low land.
Because there is so much water, almost all children learn to swim when they are about five years old.
The Delta Works [De Deltawerken]: in 1953 there was a big flood.
A large part of Zeeland, Zuid-Holland and Noord-Brabant went under water.
More than 1,800 people died.
After that, the government made a plan against the floods: the Deltaplan.
Especially in Zeeland, good dikes and dams were built: the Deltawerken.
The Oosterscheldekering is such a dam in Zeeland.
It usually stands open; it only closes when the water from the sea gets too high.
